description_en: Hua Luogeng（1910-1985）: Hua Luogeng engineered 'independent autonomy' (mode 9) as 'mathematical self-reliance under credential deficit': under the fourfold constraint of junior-high dropout, permanent leg injury, no mentor, no laboratory, he bypassed the conventional 'study-abroad-for-degree' path and self-drawn a four-stage map of 'classic text mastery → core problem self-proof → frontier literature reproduction → open problem attack', using a single paper by Xiong Qinglin as a springboard to gain admission to Tsinghua via special exam; then produced 18 papers in two years at Cambridge — one sufficient for a PhD — instead of pursuing a degree. His famous words at Cambridge, 'I came for knowledge, not for a degree', epitomize the extreme case of 'self-defining success standards, refusing to be hostage to external credentials'.

Hua Luogeng engineered 'independent autonomy' (mode 9) as self-reliance in mathematics under credential deficit: under the fourfold constraint of junior-high dropout, permanent leg injury, no mentor, and no laboratory, he bypassed the conventional 'study-abroad-for-degree' path and self-drawn a four-stage map of 'classic text mastery → core problem self-proof → frontier literature reproduction → open problem attack', gaining admission to Tsinghua via special exam with a single paper by Xiong Qinglin; then produced 18 papers in two years at Cambridge — one sufficient for a PhD — instead of pursuing a degree. He deployed 'multidisciplinary mental models' (mode 17) to distill 'analogy, induction, extremal principles, symmetry, invariants' into a reusable mathematical toolbox, translated for non-mathematicians; 'crossing the river by feeling the stones' (mode 38) to carry the golden-section/0.618 method from theory into chemical/metallurgical/agricultural sites, one-factory-one-strategy, using output-ratio as the green-light metric; and 'strategic foresight' (mode 7) to design a four-tier talent funnel of 'interest screening → ability testing → mentorship → international competition', compressing talent development from 5–8 years with the Youth Academy. These four modes interlock into a 'self-study → research → popularisation → application' transferable scientific-engineering system — the hallmark of scaling individual genius into national mathematical capacity.

case_zh: 1910-1985 年华罗庚数学思维模式全景：1910 年 11 月 12 日生于江苏金坛；1925 年因家贫退学于金坛县立初级中学，唯一文凭为初中毕业文凭，一生仅持初中学历。1929 年患伤寒致左腿终身残疾，靠手杖行走，仍坚持自学，5 年内自修完高中至大学低年级全部数学课程。1930 年在《科学》上发表《苏家驹代数五次方程式解法不可立》，被清华数学系主任熊庆来破格赏识，1931 年以馆员身份进入清华，1933 年破格升为助教，1934 年升为讲师（清华「三次破格」之一）。1936 年经维纳推荐赴剑桥，婉拒博士学位：「我来剑桥是为了求学问，不是为了得学位」；两年发表18篇论文，其中10篇发表于《Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society》《Mathematische Annalen》等顶级期刊，论文关于塔内/华林问题者被命名为「华氏定理」，哈代大为惋惜「我的著作非改不可了」。1938 年毅然放弃剑桥优遇回国，任西南联大正教授，同年在昆明吊脚楼完成《堆垒素数论》；1942 年完稿于昆明，1953 年中科院出版，俄/匈/日/德/英译本相继面世，确立中国解析数论学派地位。1950 年放弃美国伊利诺伊大学终身教授待遇回国，任清华数学系主任、1952 年任中科院数学所首任所长；1956 年《多复变函数论中典型域的调和分析》获国家自然科学一等奖。1964 年起率小分队全国推广「优选法/统筹法」(双法)，走过20多个省市，其中武汉广播听讲达60万人；1970 年国务院邀七工业部听其讲双法。1978 年创办「华罗庚数学班」、1985 年推动中科大少年班体系，设计四级人才漏斗：兴趣测试→能力测试→导师制→国际竞赛，直接培养田刚、朱熹平、陈小旭、陈景润、王元、陆启铿、万哲先、龚昇等数学领军人物。1985 年 6 月 12 日在日本东京大学讲学时因急性心肌梗塞逝世，享年74岁；被列为芝加哥科技博物馆当今世界88位数学伟人之一。
case_en: 1910–1985: A panoramic view of Hua Luogeng's thinking-mode trajectory. Born Nov 12, 1910 in Jintan, Jiangsu; in 1925 he left Jintan County Primary School due to poverty — his only formal credential was a junior-high diploma, which he carried his whole life. In 1929 he contracted typhoid and permanently injured his left leg; walking with a cane, he still persisted in self-study and completed high-school through early-undergraduate mathematics in five years on his own. In 1930 he published 'On the Impossibility of Cardano's Algebraic Solution to the Quintic' in Science magazine; Tsinghua math chair Xiong Qinglin was so impressed he gave Hua a special-admission recommendation, bringing Hua to Tsinghua as a librarian in 1931 and promoting him — on three separate occasions — from assistant (1933) to lecturer (1934). In 1936, on Wiener's recommendation, he went to Cambridge but declined a PhD: 'I came for knowledge, not for a degree'; within two years he published 18 papers (10 in top-tier journals such as Proc. London Math. Soc. and Math. Ann.), and the 'Hua–Walfisz theorem' and 'Vinogradov–Hua theorem' bear his name, with Hardy lamenting 'My paper can never be the same again'. In 1938 he returned to China (turning down Cambridge continuation), became a professor at Southwest United University, and completed The Art of the Prime Numbers in a Kunming attic in 1942 (published by the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 1953, translated into Russian, Hungarian, Japanese, German, and English); this established the Chinese school of analytic number theory. In 1950 he declined a lifelong professorship at the University of Illinois to return, becoming chair of Tsinghua's Math Department (1950) and the founding director of the Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Mathematics (1952); his 1956 paper on harmonic analysis in typical domains of several complex variables won the National Natural Science Award, First Class. Starting in 1964 he led a small team to promote the 'optimising/unifying method' nationwide, reaching over 20 provinces with a single mass broadcast lecture in Wuhan attended by 600,000 people; in 1970 he was summoned by the State Council to instruct seven ministries on the dual method. In 1978 he founded the Hua Luogeng Mathematics Class and in 1985 helped create the USTC Youth Academy, designing a four-tier funnel — interest screening → ability testing → mentorship → international competition — that directly produced mathematical leaders such as Tian Gang, Zhu Qixia, Chen Xiaoxu, Chen Jingrun, Wang Yuan, Lu Qikeng, Wan Zhexian, and Gengsheng. He passed away of acute myocardial infarction while lecturing at the University of Tokyo on June 12, 1985, at age 74; he is counted among the 88 greatest mathematicians of our time by the Chicago Museum of Science and Technology.
